Exposure Pathways and Routes
========================================================

+ Exposure pathway = source + medium + receptor

+ Exposure route = how a contaminant enters receptor
    + Dermal contact
    + Ingestion
    + Inhalation

::::: {.slideimage}
![Three black silhouettes of a person's head and torso labeled Contact, Ingestion, and Inhalation. Arrows point at the skin for contact, into the mouth and stomach for ingestion, and into the nose and lungs for inhalation.](images/routesofexposure.png){height=4.5cm}

::: {.credit}
Damalas C. 2016. Farmers' Exposure to Pesticides: Toxicity Types and Ways of Prevention. Open Access Toxics 2016, 4(1): 1.
:::
:::::

Air Pollution Sources
========================================================
::::: {.slideimage}
![Illustration of air pollution sources. Volcanoes, wildfires, agriculture, factories, towns and homes, vehicle exhaust, aeroplanes, and shipping emit primary pollutants (carbon monoxide, nitric oxide, sulphur dioxide, nitrogen dioxide, ammonia, particulates, and volatile organic compounds), which react in the atmosphere to form secondary pollutants (sulphur trioxide, nitric acid, sulphuric acid, hydrogen peroxide, ammonium, ozone, and particulates).](images/sources-of-air-pollution.jpg){height=6.2cm}

::: {.credit}
Scotland's Environment. Air quality. https://www.environment.gov.scot/our-environment/air/air-quality/
:::
:::::

Exposure Pathway
========================================================
\small
+ Sources
    + Natural: volcanic eruptions, wildfires, allergens
    + Human: energy use, transportation, industry, agriculture
+ Pollutants
    + Primary: hazardous substance emitted directly into atmosphere
        + CO    - gas, coal, or wood combustion
        + NO~x~ - fossil fuel combustion, e.g. brown haze around cities
        + SO~2~ - volcanoes and industrial coal combustion
        + PM    - particulate matter, e.g. fossil fuel combustion, brake dust, smoke
        + NH~3~ - agricultural processes, e.g. fertilizer
        + VOCs  - volatile organic compounds, e.g. benzene, toluene
        + Pb    - "anti-knocking" agent formerly added to gasoline
    + Secondary: hazardous substance formed in atmospheric reaction
        + O~3~, SO~3~, HNO~3~, H~2~SO~4~, H~2~O~2~, NH~4~^+^, PM
+ Receptors: humans and animals (each pollutant has different health effect)

Meuse Valley Fog, Belgium (1930)
========================================================
::::: {.slideimage}
![Map of the Meuse Valley, about 20 kilometers long, running from Huy in the southwest to Liège in the northeast. A dotted line marks the fog-covered area along the river, with densely populated areas shaded and markers for large factories and deaths clustered along the narrow valley floor.](images/meusemap.png){height=6.2cm}

::: {.credit}
Nemery et al. 2001. The Meuse Valley fog of 1930: an air pollution disaster. The Lancet 357(9257): 704-708.
:::
:::::

Meuse Valley Fog, Belgium (1930)
========================================================
+ Sources
    + SO~2~, H~2~SO~4~, or HF from nearby zinc, glass, and steel factories
    + Inversion: warm air layer trapped cold, polluted air in the valley (5 days in Dec)
+ Receptors
    + Asthma-like symptoms: shortness of breath, coughing fits
    + Estimated 60 excess deaths (20-89 years old)
+ Impacts
    + Seen at the time as "an unavoidable consequence of prosperity"
    + Interviewed family physicians and patients days after smog
    + First scientific proof of link between air pollution and illness and death
    + Demonstrated role of temperature inversions

Temperature Inversion
========================================================
::::: {.slideimage}
![Two-panel diagram over a city skyline. Under normal conditions, air is warmest near the ground and arrows show it rising freely. During a temperature inversion, a layer of warmer air sits above cooler air near the ground, and arrows show rising air blocked and turned back down.](images/inversion.PNG){height=6.2cm}

::: {.credit}
Understory captures evidence of temperature inversion in Kansas City. http://understoryweather.com/understory-captures-evidence-of-temperature-inversion-in-kansas-city/
:::
:::::

Donora, Pennsylvania Smog (1948)
========================================================
::::: {.slideimage}
![Black-and-white photo of Donora, Pennsylvania, with small houses and laundry lines in the foreground and mill smokestacks releasing smoke along the river valley in the background.](images/donora.jpg){height=6.2cm}

::: {.credit}
Donora Historical Society and Smog Museum. https://www.sites.google.com/site/donorahistoricalsociety/1948-smog
:::
:::::

Donora, Pennsylvania Smog (1948)
========================================================
+ Sources
    + CO, SO~2~, and H~2~SO~4~ from steel and zinc factories
    + Temperature inversion (5 days in Oct)
+ Receptors
    + About 14,000 residents trapped under thick layer of smog
    + Nearly 7,000 experienced respiratory or cardiovascular issues
    + About 20 deaths during the event
+ Impacts
    + Widely publicized around world and people acted
    + Scientists began to study link between air pollution and health
    + Helped lead to first US federal air law: Air Pollution Control Act (1955)

Great Smog of London (1952)
========================================================
::::: {.slideimage}
![Black-and-white photo of a tugboat on the River Thames in thick smog, with Tower Bridge barely visible behind it.](images/londonfog.jpg){height=6.2cm}

::: {.credit}
A tugboat on the Thames near Tower Bridge in heavy smog, 1952. Fox Photos, Getty Images. https://timedotcom.files.wordpress.com/2016/11/london-fog.jpg
:::
:::::

Great Smog of London (1952)
========================================================
+ Sources
    + Cold weather led residents to burn extra coal [SO~2~, PM] to stay warm
    + Inversion: 30-mile stagnant air mass (5 days in Dec)
+ Receptors
    + About 100,000 residents felt ill with respiratory symptoms
    + Estimated 4,000-12,000 excess deaths, mostly from bronchitis and pneumonia
+ Impacts
    + Especially bad "pea-souper" as seen on TV (e.g. *The Crown*)
    + Led to UK Clean Air Act of 1956 (and 1970 in US)
    + Landmark in air pollution epidemiology: first detailed analysis linking pollutant levels to illness and death [(Nemery et al. 2001)](https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(00)04135-0/fulltext)

Los Angeles Smog and Clean Air Act (1970)
========================================================
::::: {.slideimage}
![Photo of the downtown Los Angeles skyline under a thick brown layer of smog, with clear blue sky above the haze.](images/lasmog1.jpg){height=6.2cm}

::: {.credit}
Photochemical smog in Los Angeles. Getty images.
:::
:::::

Los Angeles Smog and Clean Air Act (1970)
========================================================
\small
+ Sources
    + 1,000,000+ vehicles on LA roads by 1940
    + VOC emissions + sunlight + NO~x~ $\rightarrow$ O~3~ (photochemical smog)
    + LA is natural trap for smog accumulation
        + Geography: flat basin between ocean and mountains
        + Weather patterns: cold ocean current creates inversions
+ Receptors
    + Respiratory and cardiovascular effects among residents
    + Systematic spatial association between respiratory mortality and increased O~3~ levels in 1961 [(Mahoney 1976)](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC1130478/?page=3)
+ Impacts
    + [Clean Air Act of 1970](https://www.epa.gov/laws-regulations/summary-clean-air-act) set federal and state regulations to limit stationary and mobile source emissions
    + O~3~ levels far below 1970s peaks despite many more cars
    + Still ranked worst US metro for O~3~ in 26 of last 27 years [(ALA State of the Air 2026)](https://www.lung.org/research/sota)

Beijing "Airpocalypse" (2013-2014)
========================================================
::::: {.slideimage}
![Two photos of the same Beijing skyline. In the top photo, smog hides most buildings in gray haze; in the bottom photo, the buildings are sharp against a clear sky.](images/beijing-smog-split-screen-horizontal-large-gallery.png){height=6.2cm}

::: {.credit}
Beijing smog vs. no smog. 2014. Getty Images.
:::
:::::

Beijing "Airpocalypse" (2013-2014)
========================================================
+ Sources
    + PM from burning coal for heat in winter, industry, and vehicle traffic
    + Like LA, Beijing in "natural bowl" with temperature inversions
+ Receptors
    + Respiratory and cardiovascular effects among residents
    + Jan 2013: PM~2.5~ went "beyond index," over 20x WHO guideline
+ Impacts
    + 2013 Air Pollution Action Plan: cut coal, closed old plants, cleaner fuels
    + Annual PM~2.5~ fell from about 100 $\mu$g/m^3^ (2013) to 27 $\mu$g/m^3^ (2025)
    + US Embassy hourly air quality posts raised public pressure

Recent Wildfire Smoke Events (2020-2025)
========================================================
\small
+ Sources
    + Hotter, drier conditions and strong winds drive larger fires
    + Smoke (mostly PM~2.5~) travels hundreds to thousands of miles
+ Receptors
    + Entire regions, rural and urban, often far from the fire
+ Some recent major wildfire smoke events
    + West Coast, Sept 2020: Portland had world's worst major-city air; daily AQI peaked at 357 (Portland) and 196 (Seattle)
    + East Coast, June 2023: smoke from Canadian fires pushed NYC AQI near 500; about 62 million people exposed
    + Los Angeles, Jan 2025: urban fires destroyed 16,000+ structures; smoke and ash carried heavy metals
+ Impacts
    + Protection relies on AQI alerts, indoor air filtration, and limiting time outdoors

Air Pollution Studies
========================================================
\small
1. [Harvard "Six Cities" Study](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJM199312093292401)
2. [Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis and Air Pollution (MESA Air), led by UW](https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736%2816%2900378-0/fulltext)
3. [UW Adult Changes in Thought Air Pollution (ACT-AP) Study: PM~2.5~ and dementia](https://deohs.washington.edu/air-pollution-aging-brain-and-alzheimers-disease)
4. [State of Global Air 2024](https://www.stateofglobalair.org/news-events/2024/new-state-global-air-report-finds-air-pollution-second-leading-risk-factor-death): air pollution linked to 8.1 million deaths (2021), 2nd leading risk factor
5. [Burke et al. 2023, *Nature*](https://news.stanford.edu/stories/2023/09/wildfire-smokes-toxic-influence): wildfire smoke erased about 1/4 of PM~2.5~ gains since 2000 in 35 states
6. Local monitoring you can check today:
    + [Puget Sound Clean Air Agency sensor map](https://map.pscleanair.gov/), [WA Ecology air quality map](https://airqualitymap.ecology.wa.gov/), [EPA AirNow Fire and Smoke Map](https://fire.airnow.gov)
7. Health effects commonly studied: mortality, respiratory disease and lung cancer, cardiovascular disease and stroke, low birthweight, dementia

Government and Policy
========================================================
\small
1. Clean Air Act (1956-UK; 1970-USA)
2. National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS)
    + CO, Pb, NO~2~, O~3~, PM~10~, PM~2.5~, SO~2~
    + 2024: annual PM~2.5~ standard lowered from 12 to 9 $\mu$g/m^3^ (upheld in federal court, 2026)
3. [WHO Air Quality Guidelines (2021)](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240034228): annual PM~2.5~ guideline of 5 $\mu$g/m^3^
4. Air quality modeling and monitoring
    + [Dispersion](https://www.epa.gov/scram/air-quality-dispersion-modeling-preferred-and-recommended-models) and [receptor](https://www.epa.gov/scram/air-pollutant-receptor-modeling) modeling; [Puget Sound Clean Air Agency](https://pscleanair.gov/) and [WA Ecology](https://airqualitymap.ecology.wa.gov/) monitors
    + [EPA Our Nation's Air 2025](https://gispub.epa.gov/air/trendsreport/2025/\#home): national air quality and emissions trends
5. [WA wildfire smoke rule for workers](https://lni.wa.gov/safety-health/safety-rules/rulemaking-stakeholder-information/wildfire-smoke) (L&I, 2024; updated 2025)
6. [WA Climate Commitment Act](https://ecology.wa.gov/Air-Climate/Climate-Commitment-Act/Overburdened-communities): improving air quality in 16 overburdened communities
